key_insight: The paper shows that an LLM agent can learn confidence signals calibrated to the eventual success of an entire multi-step episode, enabling better decide-to-act vs abstain behavior.
engineering_relevance: This matters for deploying agents in real systems because step-level confidence can support selective execution, human handoff, and safer long-horizon automation without reducing task success.
method: Use GRPO to train the agent’s verbalized confidence against the final episode outcome rather than the current-step correctness.
Apply a proper scoring rule to each rollout step using success labels from grouped trajectories.
Evaluate both offline on logged trajectories and online on a live ALFWorld agent, including selective execution metrics.
evidence_signal: Across offline ALFWorld, TextWorld, and WebShop evaluations, step confidence AUROC rises from near chance to 0.68–0.85, and in online ALFWorld calibration rewards reduce ECE from 0.42 to below 0.12.
watch_item: The strongest signal appears to be episode-level foresight rather than clean attempt-level discrimination, so real deployments should be cautious about over-trusting confidence on harder or early-step decisions.
paper_title: Can an Agent Learn to Predict Its Own Failure? Outcome-Grounded Confidence Calibration in LLM Agents
